+## AeroCement Mix Design Proposals
+
+### Mix A: High-Fly-Ash Structural (Primary)
+
+| Component | Mass Fraction | Notes |
+|-----------|--------------|-------|
+| Class F Fly Ash | 60% | Low-calcium preferred |
+| Metakaolin | 10% | Reactive Al-Si source |
+| Perlite (expanded) | 25% | Lightweight aggregate |
+| Basalt Fiber | 3% | 12mm chopped |
+| Polypropylene Fiber | 2% | 6mm chopped, fire resistance |
+
+**Activator Solution:**
+- Sodium Hydroxide: 10M solution
+- Sodium Silicate (Na₂SiO₃): modulus 2.0–2.5
+- NaOH:Na₂SiO₃ mass ratio: 1:2.5
+- Solution:Binder mass ratio: 0.35–0.40
+
+**Target Properties (Require Lab Verification):**
+- 28-day compressive strength: ≥15 MPa
+- Density: 1,400–1,600 kg/m³
+- Thermal conductivity: 0.35–0.50 W/m·K
+
+---
+
+### Mix B: Ferrocement Fallback
+
+For sites where fly ash is unavailable:
+- Portland cement: 1 part
+- Sharp sand: 1.5 parts
+- Water:cement ratio: 0.38–0.42
+- Admixture: latex polymer modifier (5% by cement weight)
+- Reinforcement: 2-layer galvanized welded mesh, 12.5mm × 12.5mm × 1.2mm wire
+
+**Properties:**
+- 28-day compressive strength: ≥25 MPa
+- Density: ~2,100 kg/m³
+- Thermal conductivity: ~1.0 W/m·K
+
+**Note:** Mix B provides structural equivalence but loses the thermal advantage. External insulation required in hot climates.

+# Black Locust as Keystone Species — Section 5.1
+
+> ⚠️ **NOTE:** Black locust is aggressive and can outcompete native species. Site-specific ecological assessment is required before large-scale planting.
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 5.1*
+
+---
+
+## Why Black Locust (*Robinia pseudoacacia*)
+
+### Nitrogen Fixation
+- Fixes 40–100 kg N/ha/year via *Rhizobium* symbiosis
+- Reduces or eliminates synthetic nitrogen fertilizer requirements
+
+### Structural Timber
+| Property | Value |
+|----------|-------|
+| Density | 770 kg/m³ |
+| Modulus of elasticity | 14–16 GPa |
+| Natural durability (EN 350) | Class 1 — 80–100 years in ground contact without treatment |
+| Compressive strength | 60–70 MPa |
+
+Suitable for framing, posts, foundation piles, and fuel.
+
+### Fodder and Apiculture
+- Flowers: monofloral honey nectar; edible for humans

+
+### Rapid Growth
+- Reaches harvestable diameter (12–15cm) in 8–12 years
+- Coppices vigorously: 20–25 year coppice rotation cycles
+
+---
+
+## Proposed Planting
+
+**Density:** 50–200 trees/acre in alley cropping configuration  
+**Annual yield (established):** 5–10 cords wood + nitrogen fertility + fodder

+
+- Honey locust (*Gleditsia triacanthos*)

+# Quail Towers — Section 5.2
+
+> ⚠️ **THEORETICAL** — Individual quail stocking densities are within industry norms. The integration of quail towers with dome thermal mass and aquaponics represents the novel system architecture.
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 5.2*
+
+---
+
+## Why Coturnix Quail (*Coturnix coturnix japonica*)
+
+| Parameter | Value |
+|-----------|-------|
+| Feed conversion ratio | 2.5:1 (feed:egg by weight) |
+| Egg production | 250–300 eggs/year per hen |
+| Space requirement | 0.05–0.1 m²/bird (>50× more efficient than chickens) |
+| Maturation | 6–8 weeks to laying age |
+| Noise | Minimal (important for urban) |
+| Disease resistance | Robust |
+
+---
+
+## Tower Design
+
+Vertical stacking of quail cages along the dome's south wall provides:
+
+1. **Passive heating** — Metabolic heat (≈5W/bird × 100 birds = 500W) in winter
+2. **CO₂ enrichment** — For attached greenhouse/aquaponics zone
+3. **Nutrient cycling** — High-nitrogen liquid waste → aquaponics input
+4. **Protein production** — In minimal footprint
+
+---
+
+## Production Targets (50 m² Tower, 500–1,000 Birds)
+
+| Output | Target |
+|--------|--------|
+| Eggs | 350–700/day |
+| Meat (culled males/excess) | 2–4 kg/week |
+| Liquid waste for aquaponics | 50–100 L/day |
+
+---
+
+## Integration Notes
+
+Quail metabolic heat is a meaningful supplement to dome heating in winter (500W = ~0.4 kWh thermal/hour). Waste nitrogen connects to aquaponics nitrogen cycle — see [Aquaponics](03_AQUAPONICS.md).
+
+---
+

+# Aquaponics Integration — Section 5.3
+
+> ⚠️ **THEORETICAL** — Aquaponics is a proven technology. The specific integration with quail waste input and gravity-fed Stirling-powered pumping is the novel aspect requiring management validation.
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 5.3*
+
+---
+
+## System Design
+
+**Coupled aquaponics combining:**
+- Tilapia (*Oreochromis niloticus*) — hardy, fast-growing, tolerant of high density
+- Leafy greens and herbs in floating raft (NFT or DWC) beds
+- Quail waste liquid as supplementary ammonia source
+
+---
+
+## Nitrogen Cycle
+
+```
+Quail Waste → NH₃ ─┐
+                    ├→ Nitrosomonas → NO₂⁻ → Nitrobacter → NO₃⁻ → Plant Uptake
+Fish Waste  → NH₃ ─┘
+```
+
+---
+
+## Target System Size (Family of 4)
+
+| Component | Size/Count |
+|-----------|-----------|
+| Fish tank | 2,000–4,000 L |
+| Grow beds | 20–40 m² |
+| Fish stocking | 40–80 tilapia |
+| Harvest cycle | 6–9 months |
+
+**Target yields:**
+- Fish: 15–25 kg/month
+- Leafy greens: 200–400g/day
+
+---
+
+## Energy Input
+
+Target: gravity-fed or air-lift pump driven by Stirling engine output.  
+Estimated pump power: 50–150W.
+
+---
+
+## Water Efficiency
+
+Aquaponics uses **90–95% less water** than soil agriculture for equivalent yield (Somerville et al., FAO 2014). This is critical in arid deployment contexts.
+
+---
+
+## Startup Protocol
+
+⚠️ **Biological cycle must be established before stocking fish.**
+
+1. Fill tank, add beneficial bacteria inoculant
+2. Run nitrogen cycle for minimum 4–6 weeks (monitor NH₃, NO₂⁻, NO₃⁻)
+3. Stock plants when cycle is confirmed stable
+4. Stock fish after plant establishment
+5. Add quail waste input gradually after system stabilizes
+
+---
+

+# Seed Banking — Section 5.4
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 5.4*
+
+---
+
+## Seed Sovereignty
+
+The ability to reproduce the entire food system from open-pollinated seed is a **core design requirement.** The AeroCement system does not rely on hybrid or patented seed stock.
+
+---
+
+## Underground Vault Design
+
+Location: 1.5m depth (uses ground temperature stability for free temperature control)
+
+**Storage Conditions (Target):**
+
+| Parameter | Target |
+|-----------|--------|
+| Temperature | 8–12°C (ground-coupled) |
+| Humidity | <40% RH (sealed mylar + desiccant) |
+| Viability target | >80% germination at 5 years |
+
+---
+
+## Recommended Seed Categories
+
+**Food crops (open-pollinated varieties):**
+- Tomato, pepper, squash, bean, corn, sunflower
+- Kale and brassicas
+- Root vegetables (carrot, beet, turnip)
+- Culinary herbs
+
+**Priority traits:**
+- Heat tolerance
+- Drought resistance
+- Landrace/heritage varieties adapted to local conditions
+
+**Cover crops and green manure:**
+- Legumes for nitrogen fixation
+- Grasses for carbon addition
+
+---
+
+## Seed Bank Maintenance
+
+- Test germination rates annually (10-seed test sample per variety)
+- Replenish from each season's harvest
+- Document variety name, source, date stored, germination test results
+- **Token issuance:** Each verified variety deposited earns SEED tokens (see [Economy](../04_ECONOMY/README.md))
+
+---

+# Proof of Physical Work — Sections 7.1–7.2
+
+*From THESIS.md Sections 7.1–7.2*
+
+---
+
+## 7.1 The Problem
+
+Existing cryptocurrency proof-of-work systems consume energy producing no useful physical output. Proof-of-stake concentrates governance in proportion to existing wealth. Neither mechanism rewards physical contribution to real-world infrastructure.
+
+---
+
+## 7.2 The Protocol
+
+**Core mechanism:**
+
+```
+Token Issuance = f(Verified_Physical_Work, Thermodynamic_Output, Peer_Attestation)
+```
+
+Where:
+- **Verified_Physical_Work** = GPS-verified labor hours + photographic documentation at each build phase
+- **Thermodynamic_Output** = measured data from instrumented dome (temperature differential, Stirling output, food production)
+- **Peer_Attestation** = multi-signature confirmation from existing node operators that build meets specifications
+
+---
+
+## BUILD Token Issuance Schedule
+
+| Milestone | BUILD Tokens |
+|-----------|-------------|
+| Foundation + Tension Ring complete | 100 |
+| Shell complete, first coat | 200 |
+| Shell complete, weathertight | 300 |
+| Systems commissioned (water, thermal) | 200 |
+| First harvest (food system operational) | 200 |
+| **Total per dome** | **1,000** |
+
+---
+
+## All Four Token Classes
+
+| Token | Issuance Trigger | Supply Cap |
+|-------|-----------------|------------|
+| BUILD | Completed dome shell milestone | 1,000 per dome |
+| THERM | Per kWh equivalent passive cooling verified | Unlimited |
+| HARVEST | Per kg food produced, certified | Unlimited |
+| SEED | Per variety in verified seed bank | 100 per variety |
+
+---
+
+## Instrumentation Requirements
+
+For token issuance, the following must be installed and logging:
+- Interior/exterior thermocouple pair (≥15-minute interval)
+- Chimney air temperature sensor
+- Supply air temperature/humidity sensor
+- Stirling output power meter
+- Water consumption meter (evaporative system)
+- GPS-tagged photographic documentation (≥weekly)
+
+---
+

+# DAO Governance — Section 7.3
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 7.3*
+
+---
+
+## Three-Tier Structure
+
+### Technical Council (TC)
+- 7 members elected by BUILD token holders
+- Responsibilities: protocol specification updates, build standard amendments, dispute resolution
+- Term: 2 years, staggered
+- Quorum: 5/7 for standard decisions, 7/7 for protocol hard forks
+
+### Build Validators (BV)
+- Elected by regional token holders
+- Conduct on-site verification for BUILD token issuance
+- **Bonded** — stake required to prevent fraudulent attestation
+- One BV per 50 domes in region
+
+### Token Holder Assembly (THA)
+- All token holders
+- Vote on: DAO treasury allocation, TC elections, ecosystem fund deployments
+- Minimum to vote: 10 BUILD or equivalent
+
+---
+
+## Treasury
+
+**10% of all BUILD token issuance → DAO treasury**
+
+Treasury funds:
+- Protocol development (open-source)
+- Build validator training
+- Seed bank maintenance
+- Emergency resilience reserves
+
+---
+
+## Governance Philosophy
+
+The DAO is designed so that:
+- Power is earned through building, not buying
+- Technical decisions require demonstrated expertise (TC)
+- On-site verification is performed by regionally accountable validators
+- All protocol changes are public and versioned
+

+# Token Economy — Overview
+
+The AeroCement token economy is a **Proof-of-Physical-Work (PoPW)** protocol that anchors cryptographic token issuance to verifiable physical labor and instrumented measurements on real AeroCement infrastructure.
+
+It solves a core problem: existing proof-of-work systems produce no useful physical output. PoPW rewards actual construction and food production.
+
+---
+
+## Four Token Classes
+
+| Token | Backed By | Supply |
+|-------|-----------|--------|
+| BUILD | Verified dome construction milestones | 1,000 per dome |
+| THERM | Verified passive cooling (kWh equivalent) | Unlimited |
+| HARVEST | Verified food production (kg) | Unlimited |
+| SEED | Verified variety in seed bank | 100 per variety |
+
+---
+
+## Documents in This Section
+
+| File | Contents |
+|------|----------|
+| [01_PROOF_OF_PHYSICAL_WORK.md](01_PROOF_OF_PHYSICAL_WORK.md) | Protocol design, token mechanics — Thesis Sections 7.1–7.2 |
+| [02_DAO_GOVERNANCE.md](02_DAO_GOVERNANCE.md) | Technical council, validators, token assembly — Thesis Section 7.3 |
+| [03_BOUNTY_SYSTEM.md](03_BOUNTY_SYSTEM.md) | Research, build, and open-source bounties — Thesis Section 7.4 |
+
+---
+
+## Design Philosophy
+
+> "We need a coordination mechanism that rewards people for building real things in the physical world."
+
+The PoPW protocol is designed so that:
+- Tokens are **meaningless** without verified physical work
+- **No one can earn tokens by speculating** — only by building or measuring
+- The more validated data the community accumulates, the more secure the protocol becomes
+

+# Hard Constraints — Section 6.1
+
+> These are **non-negotiable** design limits. Builds violating these constraints are not AeroCement-compliant and cannot earn BUILD tokens.
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 6.1*
+
+---
+
+## Structural Constraints
+
+1. **Minimum shell thickness:** 50mm for spans <6m; 75mm for 6–9m spans
+2. **Base ring continuity:** Tension ring must be continuous and closed — no gaps
+3. **Penetration framing:** All penetrations (windows, doors, chimney) must maintain continuity of tension ring
+4. **Hub connections:** Must include positive mechanical lock (bolt or wedge). **Adhesive-only connections are prohibited.**
+5. **Foundation bearing:** Must bear on undisturbed soil or engineered fill. No bearing on made ground without geotechnical assessment.
+
+## Thermal Constraints
+
+6. **Chimney cross-section:** Minimum 0.15 m² for 4–6m dome diameter
+7. **Evaporative media depth:** Minimum 100mm at design airflow velocity
+8. **Thermal mass minimum:** 200 kg/m² of floor area
+9. **Glazing:** All windows must be double-glazed or double-film. **Single-pane is prohibited** in climate zones with >40°C ambient.
+
+## Water Constraints
+
+10. **Drainage:** All water systems must have overflow and drainage directed away from foundation
+11. **Aquaponics bypass:** Must have emergency bypass to prevent fish loss during pump failure
+12. **Potable water reserve:** Minimum 200L/person emergency storage
+
+## Biological Constraints
+
+13. **No pesticide application** within 10m of aquaponics or seed bank
+14. **Waste treatment:** Composting toilet or equivalent required. No flush connection to aquaponics without triple-stage treatment.
+

+# Build Sequence — Appendix C
+
+> ⚠️ Consult a qualified structural engineer for any span >6m. Obtain local permits before construction. This protocol is guidance, not a substitute for professional advice.
+
+*From THESIS.md Appendix C*
+
+---
+
+## Pre-Construction Checklist
+
+- [ ] Site analysis: solar access, wind, soil bearing capacity, water table
+- [ ] Climate data: peak summer temperature, wet bulb, humidity, solar irradiance
+- [ ] Local material sourcing: fly ash availability, activator chemicals, mesh
+- [ ] Local authority consultation: planning and building permits
+- [ ] Foundation design verification: bearing capacity ≥50 kPa minimum
+
+---
+
+## Phase 1: Foundation and Ground Works (Weeks 1–4)
+
+- [ ] Mark out dome footprint (circle + berm access tunnel)
+- [ ] Excavate foundation ring beam (300mm wide × 400mm deep)
+- [ ] Excavate underground cisterns (2–4m³ each, below frost line)
+- [ ] Excavate earthen intake tunnel (600mm × 600mm minimum, 5–8m long)
+- [ ] Place and compact engineered fill if needed
+- [ ] Cast foundation ring beam with embedded anchor bolts (M16 minimum at 600mm centers)
+- [ ] Install base tension ring (50mm × 6mm continuous steel flat bar OR 100mm cast AeroCement ring beam)
+- [ ] Waterproof underground cisterns
+- [ ] Install cistern overflow and drainage
+- [ ] Backfill and compact berm
+
+---
+
+## Phase 2: Dome Shell (Weeks 5–12)
+
+### Option A: Hub-and-Strut with Spray/Apply
+
+- [ ] Erect geodesic strut framework (timber or steel)
+- [ ] Apply primary mesh layer (chicken wire or welded mesh)
+- [ ] Apply secondary mesh layer, overlapping 100mm minimum
+- [ ] First AeroCement coat: 15–20mm
+- [ ] **Cure under wet burlap for minimum 7 days — do not allow rapid drying**
+- [ ] Second coat: 20–25mm; cure 7 days
+- [ ] Final finish coat: 10–15mm
+- [ ] Apply waterproofing membrane
+- [ ] Apply reflective or high-emissivity coating appropriate to climate
+
+### Option B: Earthbag Form
+
+- [ ] Stack earthbags in dome form (temporary formwork)
+- [ ] Apply mesh over earthbag form
+- [ ] Apply AeroCement over mesh; cure as above
+- [ ] Remove earthbags after 14 days (use as berming or insulation)
+
+---
+
+## Phase 3: Penetrations and Fittings (Weeks 9–14)
+
+- [ ] Cut and frame door opening with continuous lintel and side jambs
+- [ ] Install window frames with thermal break
+- [ ] Fabricate and install chimney tube (steel or AeroCement with steel liner)
+- [ ] Fabricate and install evaporative media housing at intake
+- [ ] Install Stirling engine mounting brackets (vibration isolated)
+- [ ] Install all electrical conduit before any internal finishing
+
+---
+
+## Phase 4: Systems Commissioning (Weeks 13–20)
+
+- [ ] Install evaporative cooling media and water distribution header
+- [ ] Commission water supply and drainage for evaporative section
+- [ ] Mount Stirling engine; pressure-test working gas circuit
+- [ ] Wire Stirling generator to charge controller and battery bank
+- [ ] Install 12V/24V DC distribution panel
+- [ ] Flush and fill aquaponics system; establish biological nitrogen cycle (**4–6 weeks minimum before stocking fish**)
+- [ ] Install quail tower frame and hardware cloth
+- [ ] Commission water distribution to quail tower
+
+---
+
+## Phase 5: Biological Establishment (Months 5–18)
+
+- [ ] Plant black locust in alley-cropping pattern
+- [ ] Establish cover crops between alleys
+- [ ] Stock aquaponics with plants after nitrogen cycle confirmed
+- [ ] Stock aquaponics with fish after plant establishment
+- [ ] Introduce quail after quail tower commissioning complete
+- [ ] Populate seed bank from first harvest
+- [ ] Document all yields for HARVEST token issuance
+
+---
+
+## Instrumentation (Required for Token Issuance)
+
+- [ ] Install interior/exterior thermocouple pair (log at ≤15-minute intervals)
+- [ ] Install chimney air temperature sensor
+- [ ] Install supply air temperature/humidity sensor
+- [ ] Install Stirling output power meter
+- [ ] Install water consumption meter on evaporative system
+- [ ] Install aquaponics water quality sensors (pH, EC, temperature)
+- [ ] Establish photographic documentation protocol: ≥1 GPS-tagged photo per week
+
+---
+

+# Build Protocols — Overview
+
+> ⚠️ These protocols represent best-available design guidance. All builders must assess local conditions, obtain required permits, and consult qualified engineers for structural elements.
+
+---
+
+## Two Documents
+
+| File | Contents |
+|------|----------|
+| [01_HARD_CONSTRAINTS.md](01_HARD_CONSTRAINTS.md) | Non-negotiable design limits — Thesis Section 6.1 |
+| [02_BUILD_SEQUENCE.md](02_BUILD_SEQUENCE.md) | Complete phase-by-phase build protocol — Thesis Appendix C |
+
+---
+
+## Start Here
+
+**Read [01_HARD_CONSTRAINTS.md](01_HARD_CONSTRAINTS.md) first.** These are the non-negotiable limits. Builds that violate these constraints are not considered AeroCement-compliant and cannot earn BUILD tokens.
+
+Then read [02_BUILD_SEQUENCE.md](02_BUILD_SEQUENCE.md) for the complete step-by-step construction protocol.
+
+---
+
+## Safety Note
+
+This is a structural building system. Dome construction requires:
+- Qualified structural engineer review for any span >6m
+- Geotechnical assessment for foundation design in unknown soils
+- Local building permit compliance
+- Competent construction supervision
+
+**Do not build from this document alone without consulting local professionals.**

+# Defensive Publication — Section 8
+
+*From THESIS.md Section 8*
+
+---
+
+## Purpose
+
+This thesis constitutes a **defensive publication** — a formal public disclosure of intellectual property for the purpose of establishing prior art.
+
+By making the complete design, calculations, and specifications publicly available, this publication:
+
+1. **Prevents patent enclosure** of AeroCement Ecosystem concepts by any party
+2. **Establishes prior art** that invalidates any subsequent patent claims on the disclosed concepts
+3. **Places the technology in the public domain** permanently under the disclosed license
+
+**Legal Note:** Defensive publication is an established strategy used by IBM (Technical Disclosure Bulletins), Google (defensive patents), and academic institutions. The public availability of this document creates a prior art record that patent examiners must consider.
+
+---
+
+## What This Publication Covers
+
+The following **novel combinations and integrations** are disclosed (individual components are prior art):
+
+1. The integrated use of a passive stack-effect chimney as both ventilation driver and Stirling engine heat source within a geodesic geopolymer dome
+2. The specific integration of quail tower metabolic heat with dome heating load offset and aquaponics nitrogen cycling
+3. The BUILD/THERM/HARVEST/SEED token structure tied to instrumented physical measurements
+4. The combined use of fly ash geopolymer with lightweight aggregate targeting <0.5 W/m·K in a load-bearing dome shell
+5. The underground seed vault integrated with ground-coupled temperature stabilization within the dome thermal system
+
+---
+
+## Publication Record

+- **License:** CC-BY-SA 4.0 (Hardware/Documentation) | GPL v3 (Software)
+- **Version:** 3.0

+      interval: "weekly""},{"sha":"477331f12159a0e96d26d273536fc5dc1012ce38","filename":".github/workflows/ci.yml","status":"added","additions":68,"deletions":0,"changes":68,"blob_url":"https://github.com/jesseray718/Reticulum/blob/8a05b2a300dc1bc318eb1a87025b01c5377fc1b4/.github%2Fworkflows%2Fci.yml","raw_url":"https://github.com/jesseray718/Reticulum/raw/8a05b2a300dc1bc318eb1a87025b01c5377fc1b4/.github%2Fworkflows%2Fci.yml","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/jesseray718/Reticulum/contents/.github%2Fworkflows%2Fci.yml?ref=8a05b2a300dc1bc318eb1a87025b01c5377fc1b4","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+name: CI
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main, master]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  detect:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      has_node: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.has_node }}
+      has_python: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.has_python }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - id: scan
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          has_node=false
+          has_python=false
+          [[ -f package.json ]] && has_node=true
+          [[ -f requirements.txt || -f pyproject.toml ]] && has_python=true
+          echo "has_node=$has_node" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "has_python=$has_python" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  node:
+    needs: detect
+    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_node == 'true'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
+        with:
+          node-version: 20
+          cache: npm
+      - run: npm ci || npm install
+      - run: npm run lint --if-present
+      - run: npm test --if-present
+      - run: npm run build --if-present
+
+  python:
+    needs: detect
+    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_python == 'true'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.11"
+          cache: pip
+      - run: |
+          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
+          if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
+          if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then pip install .; fi
+      - run: |
+          if command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1; then ruff check .; else echo "ruff not installed, skipping"; fi
+      - run: |

+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: openrabbitai-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  assist:
+    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false

+    timeout-minutes: 15

+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - name: OpenRabbitAI advisory run
+        env:

+    directory: "/"
+    schedule:

+name: CI
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main, master]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  detect:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      has_node: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.has_node }}
+      has_python: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.has_python }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - id: scan
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          has_node=false
+          has_python=false
+          [[ -f package.json ]] && has_node=true
+          [[ -f requirements.txt || -f pyproject.toml ]] && has_python=true
+          echo "has_node=$has_node" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "has_python=$has_python" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  node:
+    needs: detect
+    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_node == 'true'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
+        with:
+          node-version: 20
+          cache: npm
+      - run: npm ci || npm install
+      - run: npm run lint --if-present
+      - run: npm test --if-present
+      - run: npm run build --if-present
+
+  python:
+    needs: detect
+    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_python == 'true'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.11"
+          cache: pip
+      - run: |
+          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
+          if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
+          if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then pip install .; fi
+      - run: |
+          if command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1; then ruff check .; else echo "ruff not installed, skipping"; fi
+      - run: |
+          if command -v pytest >/dev/null 2>&1; then pytest -q; else echo "pytest not installed, skipping"; fi"},{"sha":"126410697624691ea45c0a72f8bd4617723ab258","filename":".github/workflows/openrabbitai.yml","status":"added","additions":30,"deletions":0,"changes":30,"blob_url":"https://github.com/jesseray718/Reticulum/blob/8185a157aca7741b23c1938c7a7019a263edca30/.github%2Fworkflows%2Fopenrabbitai.yml","raw_url":"https://github.com/jesseray718/Reticulum/raw/8185a157aca7741b23c1938c7a7019a263edca30/.github%2Fworkflows%2Fopenrabbitai.yml","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/jesseray718/Reticulum/contents/.github%2Fworkflows%2Fopenrabbitai.yml?ref=8185a157aca7741b23c1938c7a7019a263edca30","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+name: OpenRabbitAI
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: openrabbitai-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  assist:
+    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    continue-on-error: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - name: OpenRabbitAI advisory run
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          OPENRABBITAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENRABBITAI_API_KEY }}
